title: Completed parameter charts preserve a chosen coefficient section
statement:
Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a nonzero commutative Noetherian regular local ring of finite Krull dimension $n\ge0$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], let $u_1,\ldots,u_n$ be a regular system of parameters [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters], and put $F=R/\mathfrak m$ [def-weil-residue-field]. Fix a ring section $c:F\to\widehat R$ of the residue map, where $\widehat R=\varprojlim_qR/\mathfrak m^q$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. For $r\ge0$, set $S=R[t_1,\ldots,t_r]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], $D=n+r$, and $v=(u_1,\ldots,u_n,t_1,\ldots,t_r)$. Choose $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,D\}$. If $J$ is empty, put $C=S$, $\mathfrak q=(v_1,\ldots,v_D)C$ and $w=(v_1,\ldots,v_D)$. Otherwise choose $a\in J$ and put
$$C=S[y_i\mid i\in J\setminus\{a\}]/(v_i-v_a y_i\mid i\in J\setminus\{a\}),\qquad \mathfrak q=(v_a,y_i\ (i\in J\setminus\{a\}),v_l\ (l\notin J))C,$$
and let $w$ be the displayed list of $D$ generators of $\mathfrak q$. The quotient $C/\mathfrak q$ is canonically $F$, so $\mathfrak q$ is maximal. Write $B=C_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and let $\widehat f:\widehat R\to\widehat B$ be the map induced by the local map $R\to B$. Then $B$ is Noetherian regular local of dimension $D$ and residue field $F$, and $\widehat f\circ c$ is a residue-field section. There is a unique continuous isomorphism of complete local $F$-algebras
$$\Theta:F[[W_1,\ldots,W_D]]\xrightarrow{\sim}\widehat B,\qquad W_i\longmapsto w_i,\quad b\longmapsto\widehat f(c(b)),$$
where formal power series mean [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Under the continuous coordinate isomorphism $F[[U_1,\ldots,U_n]]\cong\widehat R$ sending coefficients by $c$ and $U_i$ to $u_i$, the map $\widehat f$ is exactly the following substitution: coefficients are fixed; for $J=\varnothing$ all $u_i$ retain their coordinate variables; otherwise $v_a\mapsto e$, $v_i\mapsto eY_i$ for $i\in J\setminus\{a\}$, and $v_l\mapsto Z_l$ for $l\notin J$, with $e,Y_i,Z_l$ the variables corresponding to $w$. The same formulas specify the images of the adjoined $t_j$. The assertion includes $n=0$, $r=0$, and singleton $J$.

source.place: Tag 0C0S (lemma-regular-complete-containing-coefficient-field), clause (2) and its proof with prescribed coefficient field and parameter images. Agent algebraic parameter-chart comparison: polynomial origin completion followed by elimination of the relations v_i-v_a y_i; not asserted verbatim by that tag.

proof.text: Put $\mathfrak p=(u_1,\ldots,u_n,t_1,\ldots,t_r)S$ and $A=S_{\mathfrak p}$. Reduction of coefficients modulo $\mathfrak m$ followed by evaluation of all variables at zero gives $S/\mathfrak p=F$. In the nonempty-$J$ case, reduction also sends all $y_i$ to zero: the equations $v_i-v_a y_i$ then vanish. Conversely, killing the displayed generators $w$ kills every $v_i$, since $v_i=v_a y_i$ for $i\in J\setminus\{a\}$. Thus $C/\mathfrak q=F$, canonically with the given coefficient reduction. In either case $\mathfrak q$ is maximal and $B/\mathfrak qB=F$: a denominator outside $\mathfrak q$ reduces to a nonzero element of $F$, and its inverse reduces to the reciprocal. In particular $R\to B$ is local and its residue-field map is the identity on $F$.

source.place: Tag 00CO (definition-localization); polynomial evaluation and quotient universal properties, explicit calculation.

proof.text: The regular local ring $R$ is regular as a ring by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-localization]. Hence [lem-trf-polynomial-ring-regular-base] makes $S$ Noetherian regular, so $A$ is regular local. We check $\dim A=D$ without assuming that a maximal ideal always has full global dimension. By [lem-sf-noetherian-polynomial-dimension], $\dim S=n+r=D$. Choose a length-$n$ chain $P_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq P_n=\mathfrak m$ in $R$; it exists by the definition of finite Krull dimension (the last prime must be $\mathfrak m$, or appending it contradicts maximal length). In $S$ extend it to $P_0S\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak mS\subsetneq(\mathfrak m,t_1)\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq(\mathfrak m,t_1,\ldots,t_r)=\mathfrak p$. These are prime because their quotients are polynomial rings over domains, and the inclusions are strict by coefficients or by the next variable. They stay strict in $A$: for primes $P\subseteq\mathfrak p$, if $x/1$ lies in $PA$, some $s\notin\mathfrak p$ has $sx\in P$, hence $x\in P$. Conversely contraction sends any strict prime chain of $A$ to a strict chain in $S$, since membership of a fraction in a prime of $A$ is exactly membership of its numerator. Thus $D\leq\dim A\leq\dim S=D$. The images of the $D$ entries of $v$ generate the maximal ideal of $A$ and form a regular system of parameters.

source.place: Tag 0AFS (lemma-localization-of-regular-local-is-regular); Mathlib polynomial regularity and dimension leaves; explicit prime-chain computation at the origin.

proof.text: If $J=\varnothing$, then $B=A$, so Step 2 proves its dimension and regularity. Otherwise $D\geq1$. Form $H=A[y_i:i\in J\setminus\{a\}]/(v_i-v_a y_i)$ and its maximal ideal $\mathfrak h=(v_a,y_i,v_l:l\notin J)H$. Step 1 gives $H/\mathfrak h=F$. The map $C\to B$ inverts $S\setminus\mathfrak p$, because these elements have nonzero residue in $F$, so it extends to $H\to B$ and then to $H_{\mathfrak h}\to B$. Conversely $C\to H_{\mathfrak h}$ inverts every $c\notin\mathfrak q$, because its residue in $F$ is nonzero. The resulting maps $B\rightleftarrows H_{\mathfrak h}$ fix coefficients, the $y_i$, and inverses of all denominators; they are inverse. Apply [lem-trf-parameter-blowup-algebra-regular] over $A$ with the parameter list $v$: $H$ is Noetherian regular. Apply [lem-trf-parameter-blowup-coordinate-quotients] with $\epsilon=1$, $U=J\setminus\{a\}$, $K=\{1,\ldots,D\}\setminus J$, and $P=\mathfrak h$. It gives $\dim H_{\mathfrak h}=\dim F+1+(|J|-1)+(D-|J|)=D$. Therefore $B$ is Noetherian regular local of dimension $D$, and $w$ generates its maximal ideal with exactly $D$ entries.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 4.2.9, printed p.121 (PDF p.128), standard ratio charts; localization at the origin written explicitly.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian], [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring], [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal], [lem-weil-pbc-completion-regular-local], and [lem-weil-pbc-completion-dimension] to $R$ and $B$. Their completions are Noetherian complete regular local rings of dimensions $n$ and $D$, their maximal ideals are respectively $\mathfrak m\widehat R$ and $(w)\widehat B$, and their residue fields identify canonically with $F$. Thus the images of $u$ and $w$ generate the respective maximal ideals with the required number of entries. These applications use finite generation of the maximal ideals, provided by their displayed finite lists (also in dimension zero).

Let $f:R\to B$ be the local map. Since $f(\mathfrak m)\subseteq\mathfrak qB$, for each $q\geq1$ it induces $f_q:R/\mathfrak m^q\to B/(\mathfrak qB)^q$. These quotient maps commute with reduction. Define $\widehat f((x_q)_q)=(f_q(x_q))_q$ using [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]; componentwise operations show it is a ring map and that it agrees with $f$ on $R$. The kernel of the $q$th projection maps into the kernel of the $q$th target projection; [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power] identifies these kernels with the extended ideal powers, proving continuity. At level one, Step 1 says $f_1=1_F$. Therefore $\operatorname{res}_{\widehat B}\widehat f=\operatorname{res}_{\widehat R}$, and $c_B=\widehat f c$ satisfies $\operatorname{res}_{\widehat B}c_B=1_F$. In particular the original chosen section, rather than a newly chosen coefficient field, equips $\widehat B$ with its $F$-algebra structure.

source.place: Tag 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated), kernels of all projections; componentwise construction of the induced completed local map.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-regular-complete-coefficient-coordinates] first to $(\widehat B,(w)\widehat B)$ with coefficient map $c_B$ and list $w$, and then to $(\widehat R,\mathfrak m\widehat R)$ with coefficient map $c$ and list $u$. Step 4 verifies Noetherianity, completeness, regularity, dimensions and generation; Step 5 verifies the residue-field isomorphism for $c_B$, and it is assumed for $c$. We obtain continuous local $F$-algebra isomorphisms $\Theta:F[[W_1,\ldots,W_D]]\to\widehat B$ and $\Psi:F[[U_1,\ldots,U_n]]\to\widehat R$ with exactly the stated coefficient maps and variable values. Uniqueness of the homomorphism with those coefficients and variable images is [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-universal-property-complete], so in particular $\Theta$ is unique.

source.place: Tag 0C0S (lemma-regular-complete-containing-coefficient-field), clause (2) and proof, with the prescribed coefficients and parameters.

proof.text: Compute $g=\Theta^{-1}\widehat f\Psi$. For $b\in F$, the definition of $c_B$ gives $g(b)=b$. For each original parameter $u_i=v_i$ with $i\leq n$, the quotient relations in $C$ give: if $J=\varnothing$, its image is its corresponding $W$; otherwise its image is $e$ when $i=a$, is $eY_i$ when $i\in J\setminus\{a\}$, and is $Z_i$ when $i\notin J$. Each lies in the ideal $(W_1,\ldots,W_D)$ of $F[[W_1,\ldots,W_D]]$, for which this ring is adically complete [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-variables-complete]; so the power-series universal property [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-universal-property-complete] defines this substitution as a ring map, and its uniqueness clause identifies $g$ with this substitution on every series, since it agrees on coefficients and all $U_i$. Separately, for each $t_j=v_{n+j}$, the map $C\to B\to\widehat B$ followed by $\Theta^{-1}$ satisfies the identical three-case calculation using the same relation $v_i=v_a y_i$; this explains the adjoined-variable clause without treating $t_j$ as an element of $\widehat R$. If $J$ is singleton there are no ratio relations or $Y$ variables; if $n=0$ there are no $U$ variables; if $D=0$ then $J$ is empty and both completions are $F$. All formulas and uniqueness remain valid.
